title: Track A: Update config and restructure skills for ATS
description:
## Objective Update _config.yml and _data/skills.yml to target Senior Backend Engineer roles with ATS-optimized keywords. ## Context - GitHub issue: nulad/jobs#2 (Revamp resume for ATS) - This is a Jekyll resume site at https://nulad.github.io/resume - Web design (brutalist) stays as-is; we're optimizing content for ATS keyword scanning - Target role: remote Senior Backend Engineer ## Task 1: Update _config.yml File: `_config.yml` ### Changes: 1. Change `resume_title` from "Senior Software Engineer" to "Senior Backend Engineer" 2. Rewrite `resume_header_intro` to a 2-3 sentence ATS-targeted professional summary: - Mention: Senior Backend Engineer, 15+ years experience, remote-first - Key strengths: scalability, microservices, cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Azure) - Domain experience: loyalty/rewards, e-commerce, B2B, teleconferencing, enterprise - Keep it concise and keyword-rich - The intro uses HTML (it's rendered as HTML in the template), wrap in

tags ### Do NOT change: - Contact info visibility (keep `display_header_contact_info: "false"`) - Section toggles - Social links - Any other config values ## Task 2: Restructure _data/skills.yml File: `_data/skills.yml` ### Current structure (too sparse for ATS): ```yaml - skill: Language Stack description: .NET, Node.JS, PHP, Golang, Java ``` ### Rewrite to ATS-scannable categories with explicit keywords: - **Languages**: Java, Node.js, Golang, PHP, C#, .NET, VB.NET, SQL, JavaScript - **Cloud & Infrastructure**: AWS, GCP, Azure, microservices, serverless, Aurora - **Databases**: MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, MSSQL, MongoDB, Redis - **DevOps & CI/CD**: Docker, Bamboo, Bitbucket Pipelines, CI/CD, DevOps - **Frameworks & Tools**: Spring, Spring Security, Apache Struts, Express.js, SharePoint - **Methodologies**: Agile, Scrum, Kanban, unit testing, automated testing, TDD ### Important: - Keep the same YAML structure (`skill` + `description` keys) — the template iterates these - List technologies as comma-separated in the `description` field - Group logically so ATS can match keywords to categories - Include all technologies mentioned across experience entries in _data/experience.yml ## Verification - Run `bundle exec jekyll serve` and confirm the site renders correctly - Check that all skill categories display properly on the page - Verify the professional summary reads well and contains target keywords
close_reason: Updated title to Senior Backend Engineer, rewrote professional summary with ATS keywords, restructured skills into 6 keyword-rich categories

title: Track B: Rewrite experience bullets for ATS
description:
## Objective Rewrite all experience entries in _data/experience.yml with action-verb-led bullets, metrics, and tightened phrasing for ATS scanning. ## Context - GitHub issue: nulad/jobs#2 (Revamp resume for ATS) - This is a Jekyll resume site. Experience data is in _data/experience.yml - The YAML uses HTML markup in the `summary` field (rendered via Liquid template) - Each entry has: company, position, duration, summary (with HTML
    /
  • lists and

    tags) - Target role: remote Senior Backend Engineer - There are 8 experience entries spanning 2009-2025 ## Guidelines for rewriting bullets ### Action verbs — EVERY bullet must start with one: Led, Spearheaded, Migrated, Implemented, Designed, Architected, Built, Developed, Maintained, Optimized, Established, Streamlined, Mentored, Contributed, Resolved, Enhanced, Delivered, Consolidated, Upgraded, Automated ### Metrics — highlight wherever present: - GetPlus: "hundreds of millions rupiah" → keep specific, e.g. "disbursing hundreds of millions IDR monthly" - GetPlus: "90% of vendors" → keep - GetPlus: "tens of thousands of ecommerce transactions" → keep - GetPlus: "millions of revenue monthly" → keep - Trilogy/Jive: "multiple Jive systems into a single platform" → quantify if possible - Add approximate team sizes, system scale, or user counts where inferable ### Tighten phrasing: - Remove filler phrases like "Was involved in", "Took on the responsibility of", "During my tenure" - Remove "Notable achievements include" — just state the achievement - Cut passive constructions: "Was actively involved" → "Developed" / "Built" - Each bullet should be 1-2 lines max, not a paragraph - Keep the company description paragraph but make it 1 line max ### Tech stack: - Keep the "Tech Stack used:" paragraph at the end of each entry - Ensure tech names are consistent (Node.js not Node.JS, C# not c#) ### Structure to preserve: ```yaml - company: Company Name position: Title duration: Start — End summary: >

    One-line company description.

    • Action-verb bullet with metrics and impact
    • Another achievement bullet

    Tech Stack used: Tech1, Tech2, Tech3

    ``` ### Per-company notes: **Trilogy (2024-2025)**: Focus on platform consolidation, modernization. Emphasize Java/Spring/AWS. **GetPlus (2019-2024)**: Richest in metrics. Emphasize Azure→AWS migration, monolith→microservices, payment systems, affiliate marketing integration. **Shopee (2019)**: Short stint. Keep concise — 2 bullets max. **Bizzy (2018-2019)**: Emphasize pub-sub async architecture, microservice design. **Errai Pasifik/LoopUp (2013-2018)**: Longest tenure. Emphasize Outlook client ownership, mentorship, DevOps. **Mitrais (2011-2013)**: Keep brief — enterprise software maintenance. **Imtel (2011)**: Keep brief — data transformation, enterprise. **PLN (2009-2010)**: Keep brief — SharePoint knowledge management. ## Verification - Run `bundle exec jekyll serve` and confirm experience section renders correctly - Every bullet starts with an action verb - No bullet exceeds ~2 lines - All HTML structure is valid (proper
      /
    • /

      nesting) - Tech stack paragraph present for every entry
close_reason: Rewrote all 8 experience entries with action verbs, metrics, tighter phrasing, and ATS keywords

title: Track C: ATS-friendly print styles and layout
description:
## Objective
Update the layout template and print styles so the resume prints/exports as a clean, ATS-readable PDF.

## Context
- GitHub issue: nulad/jobs#2 (Revamp resume for ATS)
- Jekyll resume site with brutalist design (thick borders, black headers, monospace font)
- Web design stays as-is — we only modify print/PDF output
- Contact info is already print-only (user preference, do NOT change this)
- The professional summary (executive-summary div) is currently hidden in print — needs to be visible
- Browser "Print to PDF" is the export method

## Task 1: Make summary visible in print
File: `_layouts/resume.html` (line 38)

### Current:
```html
<div class="executive-summary no-print" itemprop="description">
```

### Change to:
```html
<div class="executive-summary" itemprop="description">
```

Remove the `no-print` class so the professional summary appears in printed/PDF output.

### Also make the job title visible in print:
The title-bar div (line 29) has `no-print`. The job title "Senior Backend Engineer" should be visible in print. Either:
- Remove `no-print` from the title-bar div and add `no-print` only to the icon-links include inside it, OR
- Create a separate print-only title element

Choose the cleanest approach. The title should appear between the name and contact info in print.

## Task 2: Simplify print styles for ATS
File: `_sass/_resume.scss` (print styles start at line 286)

### Changes needed:

1. **Remove decorative borders from print**: Currently resume-item has `border: 1px solid #000000`. Remove borders from `.content-section .resume-item` in print — ATS parsers can misinterpret bordered boxes as tables/columns.

2. **Remove background from section headings in print**: The `h2` in `.section-header` still has `background: #000000; color: #ffffff` in print (line 348). Make headings plain text: black text, no background, just a simple bottom border or bold text.

3. **Standard bullet characters**: Check if any CSS pseudo-elements inject special characters like "■" for list items. If so, override in print to use standard disc bullets or no custom content.

4. **Executive summary print styles**: Add styles for `.executive-summary` in the `@media print` block:
   - Font size: ~11px (slightly larger than body 10px for emphasis)
   - Line height: 1.4
   - Margin bottom: 0.5rem
   - Keep it compact but readable

5. **Ensure section order is logical for ATS**: Name → Title → Contact → Summary → Experience → Education → Skills → Social Links. (This is already the DOM order, just verify nothing gets reordered by CSS.)

6. **Clean up padding/margins**: Reduce excessive spacing in print to fit more content per page while remaining readable.

### Print styles to keep:
- `.no-print` / `.print-only` behavior
- Font size reductions
- Page break support

## Task 3: Document PDF export in the GitHub issue
After changes are made, add a comment to https://github.com/nulad/jobs/issues/2 documenting:
- How to export: Open site → Ctrl+P → Save as PDF
- Recommended settings: Letter/A4, no headers/footers, no background graphics
- Note that print styles automatically produce ATS-friendly output

## Files to modify
- `_layouts/resume.html` — remove no-print from executive-summary, handle title visibility
- `_sass/_resume.scss` — print style changes (within @media print block only)

## Verification
- Run `bundle exec jekyll serve`
- Open browser Print Preview (Ctrl+P)
- Confirm: summary visible, title visible, contact info visible, single column, no decorative borders, standard bullets, clean headings
- Confirm web version is UNCHANGED (brutalist design intact)
- Save as PDF and visually inspect
close_reason: Made title/summary visible in print, stripped decorative borders/backgrounds from print CSS, improved spacing and readability for ATS-friendly PDF output

   - Hover state performance

2. Firefox:
   - Font stack fallback
   - Border rendering
   - Print functionality

3. Safari:
   - ui-monospace support
   - Border rendering
   - Mobile Safari behavior

4. Edge:
   - Compatibility with Chrome
   - Print preview

KEY AREAS TO TEST:
- Font stack falls back correctly
- Border widths render consistently
- Hover states work instantly
- Print styles apply correctly
- Responsive breakpoints trigger

POTENTIAL ISSUES & SOLUTIONS:
- Font rendering: Add fallbacks
- Border variations: Use explicit values
- Transition removal: Ensure !important
- Print styles: Browser-specific prefixes

- Local browser testing
- Print to PDF from each browser
